seats.label: Ai(2)-mm-edgar-vampires
seats.archetype: Mardu Vampire typal go-wide linear aggro that kills by trigger rather than by combat: Edgar's eminence mints a body for every Vampire spell cast from the command zone, token multipliers stack on every mint, and SEVEN converters turn creature traffic into life loss from two directions at once — five entry payoffs (Purphoros, God of the Forge, Impact Tremors, Warleader's Call, Corpse Knight, Witty Roastmaster) that fire when a body arrives, and two death drains (Blood Artist, Cruel Celebrant) that fire when a body leaves, so a resolved board wipe pays the pilot instead of ending the game. Combat is the second kill through the lord-and-anthem layer; two checker-passed lifegain/lifeloss infinites (Bloodthirsty Conqueror with Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose or with Sanguine Bond; stacks 004 and 006) are a bonus route that assembles unassisted in 4.8% of games and is priced accordingly. The deck runs zero graveyard content by design, and the 99 is held fixed for a piloting-practice period, so this frame is a playing guide, not a shopping list.

seats.label: Ai(3)-mm-yawgmoth-swarm
seats.archetype: Mono-black aristocrats-combo: a sacrifice engine that draws while it assembles and closes with one of six rules-verified drain lines — two unbounded, one mandatory and finite-but-lethal, two library-bounded, and one rotation-engine primary that is measured rather than argued.

seats.label: Ai(4)-mm-heliod
seats.archetype: WU forced-draw punisher control: symmetric table draw made asymmetric three ways (Heliod's per-draw cost reduction, the hand-size upkeep punishers, and the Rhystic/Tithe tax layer), a two-effect pillow shell buying the waiting turns, eight counterspells defending them — and above all of it a four-card Aetherflux Reservoir storm kill that is rules-verified and rare: 0.7% of goldfish games assemble it, so the kill is the deck's ceiling and the upkeep clock is its median

scenario.question: Resolve the combat damage step. For each blocked attacker, state the minimum combat damage it must assign to its remaining blocker(s) before trampling over, given that it has deathtouch, and how much tramples to seat-3; for Craterhoof Behemoth specifically, say how its damage is assigned now that one of its two blockers (Zombie Token 449) has left the battlefield before damage. Add the unblocked attackers. Total the combat damage seat-3 takes this step and state whether 16 life survives.

steps.action: Action 1 (you, declare attackers step, turn 33): declare all eleven creatures you control — Craterhoof Behemoth, Saryth, the Viper's Fang, Fauna Shaman, Selvala, Heart of the Wilds, Beast Whisperer, Radagast of Rhosgobel, Hornet Queen and four Insect tokens — attacking seat-3 (yawgmoth-swarm, 16 life).
steps.effect: Attack legality under CR 508.1a has two halves. (i) All eleven are untapped. (ii) Each must either have haste or have been controlled by you continuously since the turn began: Craterhoof Behemoth entered THIS turn (extras.assumptions: 'entered this precombat main'), so it has NOT been under your control since the turn began and may attack only because its oracle text is 'Haste' — a static ability that lifts the 'summoning sickness' restriction of CR 302.6 for attacking. For the other ten attackers the reconstruction records summoning_sick as null (extras.reconstruction_notes: 'a creature's summoning sickness is not reconstructed'), so their eligibility is a logged action taken as given — the engine declared the attack, which it could only do if each had been under your control since the turn began (Hornet Queen and her four Insects, Fauna Shaman, Selvala, Beast Whisperer, Radagast and Saryth have no haste). Per extras.assumptions, taken as given, Craterhoof's ETB resolved this precombat main with X = 11, so its until-end-of-turn effect is still in force: each creature you control has trample and +11/+11. The attackers become tapped as a consequence of attacking. Saryth's static then applies — her oracle text reads 'Other tapped creatures you control have deathtouch', so the OTHER ten attackers have deathtouch and Saryth herself does NOT (the scenario assumption paraphrases this as 'tapped creatures you control have deathtouch'; the oracle word 'Other' excludes her). Hornet Queen and the Insect tokens have deathtouch printed anyway ('four 1/1 green Insect creature tokens with flying and deathtouch'). Resulting attackers: Craterhoof Behemoth 16/16 trample deathtouch haste; Saryth 14/15 trample (no deathtouch); Fauna Shaman 13/13, Selvala 13/14, Beast Whisperer 13/14, Radagast 13/16, Hornet Queen 13/13 — all trample deathtouch; four Insect tokens 12/12 flying trample deathtouch.

citations.quote: The active player chooses which creatures that they control, if any, will attack. The chosen creatures must be untapped, they can’t also be battles, and each one must either have haste or have been controlled by the active player continuously since the turn began.
Haste is a static ability.
If a creature has haste, it can attack even if it hasn’t been controlled by its controller continuously since their most recent turn began.
A creature can’t attack unless it has been under its controller’s control continuously since their most recent turn began. This rule is informally called the “summoning sickness” rule.
The active player taps the chosen creatures. Tapping a creature when it’s declared as an attacker isn’t a cost; attacking simply causes creatures to become tapped.
A continuous effect generated by the resolution of a spell or ability lasts as long as stated by the spell or ability creating it (such as “until end of turn”).
Deathtouch is a static ability.

steps.action: Declare attackers step, priority round: you receive priority after attackers are declared; nothing is put on the stack (the scenario's assumptions say the Elemental Bond / Beast Whisperer / Selvala draw triggers are irrelevant here, and none of them triggers on attacking). All four players pass in succession with an empty stack.
steps.effect: The declare attackers step ends and the game proceeds to the declare blockers step.

citations.quote: Second, the active player gets priority.

If all players pass in succession (that is, if all players pass without taking any actions in between passing), the spell or ability on top of the stack resolves or, if the stack is empty, the phase or step ends.
A phase or step in which players receive priority ends when the stack is empty and all players pass in succession.

steps.action: Action 2 (seat-3, declare blockers step): seat-3 declares seven blockers — Zombie Token (449) and Grave Titan both block Craterhoof Behemoth; Zombie Token (450) blocks Saryth; Pitiless Plunderer blocks Fauna Shaman; Skinrender blocks Selvala; Ayara, First of Locthwain blocks Beast Whisperer; Yawgmoth, Thran Physician blocks Radagast of Rhosgobel.
steps.effect: All seven blockers are untapped creatures seat-3 controls and each blocks one creature attacking seat-3, so the declaration is legal. Craterhoof Behemoth is a blocked creature with two blockers; Saryth, Fauna Shaman, Selvala, Beast Whisperer and Radagast are each blocked by exactly one creature; Hornet Queen and the four Insect tokens (all flying — seat-3 controls nothing with flying or reach) have no blockers declared and are unblocked creatures. Yawgmoth's protection from Humans is not an issue for his block: Radagast of Rhosgobel is an Avatar Wizard, not a Human, so no damage to Yawgmoth will be prevented.

citations.quote: The defending player chooses which creatures they control, if any, will block. The chosen creatures must be untapped and they can’t also be battles. For each of the chosen creatures, the defending player chooses one creature for it to block that’s attacking that player, a planeswalker they control, or a battle they protect.
An attacking creature with one or more creatures declared as blockers for it becomes a blocked creature; one with no creatures declared as blockers for it becomes an unblocked creature.
A creature with flying can’t be blocked except by creatures with flying and/or reach.
Any damage that would be dealt by sources that have the stated quality to a permanent or player with protection is prevented.

steps.action: Action 3 (seat-3, declare blockers step, after blocks are declared): you receive priority first and pass, seat-2 passes, and seat-3 activates Ayara, First of Locthwain's activated ability, paying {T} (tapping Ayara) and sacrificing Zombie Token (449) — one of Craterhoof Behemoth's two blockers. Ayara's oracle text is '{T}, Sacrifice another black creature: Draw a card.' The sacrificed Zombie is a black creature (Grave Titan makes '2/2 black Zombie creature tokens'), so the cost is payable.
steps.effect: The ability goes on the stack. Its costs are paid on activation: Zombie Token (449) leaves the battlefield and is therefore removed from combat — it stops being a blocking creature. Craterhoof Behemoth nonetheless REMAINS a blocked creature: a creature stays blocked even if one (or all) of its blockers is removed from combat, and Grave Titan is still blocking it. Tapping Ayara does NOT remove her from combat and does not prevent her combat damage: she is still blocking Beast Whisperer. Note the scenario's action text reads 'You gain 1 life and draw a card'; the card's oracle ability only draws a card (the life gain belongs to Ayara's separate enters trigger, which is not what is being activated). Ayara's ability itself moves no life total (it draws; it does not gain life), so the scenario's implied 17 never happens — but seat-3 does NOT stay at 16 through this step: the draw it produces triggers seat-4's Scrawling Crawler (triggers in step 5, resolves in step 6), and seat-3 enters the combat damage step at 15. Also noted, outside this question's domain: the Zombie dying triggers Pitiless Plunderer ('Whenever another creature you control dies, create a Treasure token') for seat-3 and seat-2's Blood Artist ('target player loses 1 life and you gain 1 life'); both triggers go on the stack above Ayara's ability the next time a player would receive priority and resolve first. Blood Artist's target is seat-2's choice and is not recorded — if seat-2 chose seat-3, seat-3 would be at 14 rather than 15 going into damage; neither figure changes the outcome below. Blood Artist's own 'you gain 1 life' is unconditional: seat-2 goes 43 → 44 when it resolves, and if its target was any opponent, that opponent's loss also triggers seat-2's Bloodthirsty Conqueror ('Whenever an opponent loses life, you gain that much life') for a further 1 — the target is unrecorded, so seat-2's figure from here on is a stated minimum.

citations.quote: A player may activate an activated ability any time they have priority.
To activate an ability is to put it onto the stack and pay its costs, so that it will eventually resolve and have its effect.
A permanent is removed from combat if it leaves the battlefield
A creature that’s removed from combat stops being an attacking, blocking, blocked, and/or unblocked creature.
A creature remains blocked even if all the creatures blocking it are removed from combat.
Tapping or untapping a creature that’s already been declared as an attacker or blocker doesn’t remove it from combat and doesn’t prevent its combat damage.
Once an ability has triggered, its controller puts it on the stack as an object that’s not a card the next time a player would receive priority.

steps.action: Actions 4–5: seat-3 (who receives priority after activating) passes; seat-4, you and seat-2 pass in turn (the scenario lists seat-3's pass and yours; the other two seats' passes are implied by the ability resolving). The triggered abilities above Ayara's ability resolve first — Pitiless Plunderer (seat-3 creates a Treasure), then Blood Artist (its target loses 1 life, seat-2 gains 1 life: 43 → 44) — with you, the active player, receiving priority after each resolution and all passing again; then Ayara's ability resolves: seat-3 draws a card.
steps.effect: Seat-3's hand grows by one (plus a Treasure token from Pitiless Plunderer). Ayara's ability gains no life. But the draw is a game event that matches the trigger condition of Scrawling Crawler, which seat-4 (heliod) controls — oracle: 'Whenever an opponent draws a card, that player loses 1 life' — and seat-3 is seat-4's opponent, so the Crawler's ability triggers as seat-3 draws. It is mandatory and has no target; seat-4 puts it on the stack the next time a player would receive priority, i.e. immediately after Ayara's ability finishes resolving and before you (the active player) receive priority. The stack is therefore NOT yet empty and the declare blockers step does not end here.

citations.quote: If a player has priority when they cast a spell, activate an ability, or take a special action, that player receives priority afterward.

If all players pass in succession (that is, if all players pass without taking any actions in between passing), the spell or ability on top of the stack resolves or, if the stack is empty, the phase or step ends.
The active player receives priority after a spell or ability (other than a mana ability) resolves.
Whenever a game event or game state matches a triggered ability’s trigger event, that ability automatically triggers. The ability doesn’t do anything at this point.
Once an ability has triggered, its controller puts it on the stack as an object that’s not a card the next time a player would receive priority.
If an effect causes a player to gain life or lose life, that player’s life total is adjusted accordingly.

steps.action: Declare blockers step, continued: Scrawling Crawler's triggered ability is on the stack (seat-4's). You receive priority and pass; seat-2, seat-3 and seat-4 pass in succession; the ability resolves.
steps.effect: Seat-3 loses 1 life: 16 → 15 (14 if Blood Artist's unrecorded target in step 4 was seat-3). That loss of life is itself a game event matching the trigger condition of Bloodthirsty Conqueror, which seat-2 (edgar-vampires) controls — oracle: 'Whenever an opponent loses life, you gain that much life. (Damage causes loss of life.)' — and seat-3 is seat-2's opponent, so the Conqueror's ability triggers. Mandatory, untargeted; seat-2 puts it on the stack the next time a player would receive priority — after the Crawler's ability has finished resolving, before you receive priority.

citations.quote: If all players pass in succession (that is, if all players pass without taking any actions in between passing), the spell or ability on top of the stack resolves or, if the stack is empty, the phase or step ends.
If an effect causes a player to gain life or lose life, that player’s life total is adjusted accordingly.
Whenever a game event or game state matches a triggered ability’s trigger event, that ability automatically triggers. The ability doesn’t do anything at this point.
Once an ability has triggered, its controller puts it on the stack as an object that’s not a card the next time a player would receive priority.

steps.action: Declare blockers step, continued: Bloodthirsty Conqueror's triggered ability is on the stack (seat-2's). You receive priority and pass; all others pass in succession; it resolves. Then all four players pass again with an empty stack.
steps.effect: Seat-2 gains 1 life — 'that much' is the 1 seat-3 lost. Seat-2's running total: 43 + 1 (Blood Artist's gain) + 1 (Conqueror on the Crawler loss) = 45, and 46 if Blood Artist's unrecorded target was an opponent (every sensible choice) — so seat-2 enters the combat damage step at AT LEAST 45. Seat-3 enters it at 15 (14 if Blood Artist targeted seat-3). With the stack empty and every player passing in succession, the declare blockers step ends and the combat damage step begins. No attacking or blocking creature has first strike or double strike (Craterhoof Behemoth's printed keyword is Haste; none of the other ten attackers nor any of the six remaining blockers has either), so there is a single combat damage step.

citations.quote: If all players pass in succession (that is, if all players pass without taking any actions in between passing), the spell or ability on top of the stack resolves or, if the stack is empty, the phase or step ends.
If an effect causes a player to gain life or lose life, that player’s life total is adjusted accordingly.
A phase or step in which players receive priority ends when the stack is empty and all players pass in succession.

If at least one attacking or blocking creature has first strike (see rule 702.7) or double strike (see rule 702.4) as the combat damage step begins, the only creatures that assign combat damage in that step are those with first strike or double strike.

steps.action: Combat damage step, first part: you (active player) announce how each attacking creature assigns its combat damage, then seat-3 announces how each blocking creature assigns its combat damage. Each creature assigns damage equal to its power. For each trampling attacker, lethal damage must be assigned to every creature still blocking it before any damage goes to seat-3; where the attacker has deathtouch, 1 damage counts as lethal.
steps.effect: Minimum-to-blocker assignments (maximum trample-through): CRATERHOOF BEHEMOTH (16 power, trample, deathtouch) — blocked, but Zombie Token (449) is no longer blocking it; exactly ONE creature, Grave Titan (6/6), is blocking it, so all damage it assigns to blockers goes to Grave Titan. Because Craterhoof has deathtouch, 1 damage assigned to Grave Titan is lethal damage; the remaining 15 may be assigned to seat-3. (Rule 702.19d — damage assigned 'as though all blocking creatures have been assigned lethal damage' — does NOT apply, because one blocker remains; the removal of 449 simply means there is no second blocker to satisfy.) Assignment: 1 to Grave Titan, 15 to seat-3. SARYTH, THE VIPER'S FANG (14 power, trample, NO deathtouch — her own ability reads 'Other tapped creatures') — blocked by Zombie Token (450), a 2/2; lethal damage is 2 (its toughness). Assignment: 2 to Zombie Token (450), 12 to seat-3. (Had she deathtouch as the scenario assumption implies, it would be 1 and 13.) FAUNA SHAMAN (13, trample, deathtouch) blocked by Pitiless Plunderer (1/4): 1 to Plunderer, 12 to seat-3. SELVALA, HEART OF THE WILDS (13, trample, deathtouch) blocked by Skinrender (3/3): 1 to Skinrender, 12 to seat-3. BEAST WHISPERER (13, trample, deathtouch) blocked by Ayara (2/3, tapped but still blocking): 1 to Ayara, 12 to seat-3. RADAGAST OF RHOSGOBEL (13, trample, deathtouch) blocked by Yawgmoth (2/4): 1 to Yawgmoth, 12 to seat-3 (Radagast is not a Human, so protection from Humans prevents nothing). HORNET QUEEN (13) unblocked: 13 to seat-3. FOUR INSECT TOKENS (12 each) unblocked: 12 each, 48 to seat-3. Blockers assign back: Grave Titan 6 (deathtouch) to Craterhoof Behemoth; Zombie Token (450) 2 to Saryth; Pitiless Plunderer 1 to Fauna Shaman; Skinrender 3 to Selvala; Ayara 2 to Beast Whisperer; Yawgmoth 2 to Radagast. Total combat damage assigned to seat-3: 15 + 12 + 12 + 12 + 12 + 12 + 13 + 48 = 136.

citations.quote: First, the active player announces how each attacking creature assigns its combat damage, then the defending player announces how each blocking creature assigns its combat damage. This turn-based action doesn’t use the stack.
Each attacking creature and each blocking creature assigns combat damage equal to its power.

A blocked creature assigns its combat damage to the creatures blocking it. If no creatures are currently blocking it (if, for example, they were destroyed or removed from combat), it assigns no combat damage. If exactly one creature is blocking it, it assigns all its combat damage to that creature.

The controller of an attacking creature with trample first assigns damage to the creature(s) blocking it. Once all those blocking creatures are assigned lethal damage, any excess damage is assigned as its controller chooses among those blocking creatures and the player, planeswalker, or battle the creature is attacking.

If an attacking creature with trample or trample over planeswalkers is blocked, but there are no creatures blocking it when damage is assigned, its damage is assigned to the defending player and/or planeswalker as though all blocking creatures have been assigned lethal damage.
Any nonzero amount of combat damage assigned to a creature by a source with deathtouch is considered to be lethal damage for the purposes of determining if excess damage is being dealt.
An amount of damage greater than or equal to a creature’s toughness.
An unblocked creature assigns its combat damage to the player, planeswalker, or battle it’s attacking.
A blocking creature assigns combat damage to the creatures it’s blocking.
Any damage that would be dealt by sources that have the stated quality to a permanent or player with protection is prevented.

steps.action: Combat damage step, second part: all assigned combat damage is dealt simultaneously; no player may act between assignment and dealing.
steps.effect: Seat-3 is dealt 136 combat damage and loses 136 life: 15 − 136 = −121 (−122 if Blood Artist had targeted seat-3 in step 4). That 136-point loss of life is a game event matching Bloodthirsty Conqueror's trigger condition — seat-3 is seat-2's opponent — so the Conqueror's ability triggers for seat-2 at this moment; it waits to be put on the stack (step 11) because no player receives priority between damage being dealt and the state-based action check. Damage is marked on the creatures: Grave Titan 1 (from a deathtouch source), Zombie Token (450) 2, Pitiless Plunderer 1, Skinrender 1, Ayara 1, Yawgmoth 1 (each from a deathtouch source); Craterhoof Behemoth 6 (from Grave Titan, a deathtouch source), Saryth 2, Fauna Shaman 1, Selvala 3, Beast Whisperer 2, Radagast 2.

citations.quote: Second, all combat damage that’s been assigned is dealt simultaneously. This turn-based action doesn’t use the stack. No player has the chance to cast spells or activate abilities between the time combat damage is assigned and the time it’s dealt.
Damage dealt to a player by a source without infect causes that player to lose that much life.
Damage marked on a creature remains until the cleanup step, even if that permanent stops being a creature.
Whenever a game event or game state matches a triggered ability’s trigger event, that ability automatically triggers. The ability doesn’t do anything at this point.

steps.action: Combat damage step, third part: before you would receive priority, state-based actions are checked and performed as a single event.
steps.effect: Seat-3 has −121 life (−122 at worst) and loses the game. Simultaneously, every blocker that was dealt damage by a deathtouch source is destroyed (Grave Titan, Pitiless Plunderer, Skinrender, Ayara, Yawgmoth), Zombie Token (450) is destroyed by lethal damage (2 on a 2/2), and Craterhoof Behemoth is destroyed — it was dealt 6 damage by Grave Titan, a source with deathtouch, so its 16 toughness does not save it. Because seat-3 has left the game, all objects seat-3 owns leave the game with them. Your other attackers survive: Saryth (2 marked on 15 toughness), Fauna Shaman (1 on 13), Selvala (3 on 14), Beast Whisperer (2 on 14), Radagast (2 on 16), Hornet Queen and the Insects undamaged. ANSWER: seat-3 takes 136 combat damage this step; 16 life does not survive — it does not survive at the 15 seat-3 actually holds after Scrawling Crawler, nor at the scenario's 16, nor at the scenario's mis-stated 17 (after a life gain Ayara's ability does not actually grant) and at the 15 it actually holds, Craterhoof's 15 trample-through alone is lethal (15 − 15 = 0 loses under 704.5a), any one of the 12s alone leaves it at 3, and any two attackers together are lethal; at the scenario's 16 or 17 no single attacker is lethal but any two are. Any 'you' net: Craterhoof Behemoth is lost to Grave Titan's deathtouch in the exchange. Before you receive priority, the triggered abilities that are waiting go on the stack (step 11).

citations.quote: Whenever a player would get priority (see rule 117, “Timing and Priority”), the game checks for any of the listed conditions for state-based actions, then performs all applicable state-based actions simultaneously as a single event.
If a player has 0 or less life, that player loses the game.
If a creature has toughness greater than 0, and it’s been dealt damage by a source with deathtouch since the last time state-based actions were checked, that creature is destroyed.

If a creature has toughness greater than 0, it has damage marked on it, and the total damage marked on it is greater than or equal to its toughness, that creature has been dealt lethal damage and is destroyed.
When a player leaves the game, all objects (see rule 109) owned by that player leave the game
Third, the active player gets priority.

steps.action: Combat damage step, after state-based actions and before you receive priority: the waiting triggered abilities are put on the stack. Seat-2 controls Bloodthirsty Conqueror's trigger (seat-3's 136-point loss) and seven Blood Artist triggers ('Whenever this creature or another creature dies, target player loses 1 life and you gain 1 life') — one each for Grave Titan, Zombie Token (450), Pitiless Plunderer, Skinrender, Ayara, Yawgmoth and Craterhoof Behemoth, all of which died in the single SBA event — and puts them on the stack in any order seat-2 chooses (you, the active player, have no triggers; seat-4 has none). Pitiless Plunderer's own death triggers would be controlled by seat-3, who has left the game, so they are not put on the stack. Taking the Conqueror trigger as the one in this question's domain: you receive priority, all pass, it resolves.
steps.effect: Seat-2 gains 136 life — 'that much' is the 136 seat-3 lost to combat damage. Seat-2's life is therefore AT LEAST 45 + 136 = 181 (182 if Blood Artist's step-4 target was an opponent) — NOT unchanged by combat. The seven Blood Artist death triggers then follow: each gains seat-2 another 1 and makes its target (seat-2's choice; with seat-3 gone the opponents are you at 12 and seat-4 at 13) lose 1, and each such opponent loss triggers the Conqueror again for 1 more — those targets are unrecorded and outside this question's domain, so seat-2's final figure is reported as a floor. You are at 12 when the combat damage step's first priority is reached — or 11 if Blood Artist's unrecorded step-4 target was you — and seat-4 is at 13, or 12 if that same unrecorded target was seat-4: the step-4 Blood Artist trigger made exactly one player lose 1, and the scenario does not record which, so you and seat-4 are each a ceiling in the same way seat-3 (15 or 14) and seat-2 (45 or 46) were hedged above; nothing else in this question's domain lowers either.

citations.quote: If any state-based actions are performed as a result of a check, the check is repeated; otherwise all triggered abilities that are waiting to be put on the stack are put on the stack, then the check is repeated.
Once an ability has triggered, its controller puts it on the stack as an object that’s not a card the next time a player would receive priority.
First, each player, in APNAP order, puts each triggered ability they control with a trigger condition that isn’t another ability triggering on the stack in any order they choose.
If a triggered ability that would be controlled by a player who has left the game would be put onto the stack, it isn’t put on the stack.
Third, the active player gets priority.

If all players pass in succession (that is, if all players pass without taking any actions in between passing), the spell or ability on top of the stack resolves or, if the stack is empty, the phase or step ends.
If an effect causes a player to gain life or lose life, that player’s life total is adjusted accordingly.

final_state.summary: Seat-3 (yawgmoth-swarm) takes 136 combat damage in a single combat damage step — Craterhoof 15 (1 to its one remaining blocker Grave Titan, deathtouch making 1 lethal), Saryth 12 (2 to Zombie 450: Saryth has NO deathtouch, her text grants it only to OTHER tapped creatures), Fauna Shaman / Selvala / Beast Whisperer / Radagast 12 each (1 to each deathtouch-lethal blocker), Hornet Queen 13 and four Insects 48 unblocked — and goes from 15 to −121; 16 life does not survive (seat-3 was in fact at 15 when damage was dealt: the card it drew off Ayara cost it 1 life to seat-4's Scrawling Crawler during the declare blockers step) and seat-3 loses the game as a state-based action. Sacrificing Zombie 449 to Ayara did not unblock Craterhoof (CR 509.1h) and did not make 702.19d apply (one blocker remained); it changed Craterhoof's minimum blocker assignment from 2 to 1 and its trample-through from 14 to 15. Craterhoof may attack the turn it entered because it has printed Haste (CR 508.1a, 702.10b). Two scenario-vs-oracle disagreements found and resolved by oracle text: Ayara's activated ability draws a card and does not gain life (no 17); Saryth's deathtouch grant says 'Other', so her own assignment is 2/12 not 1/13. Neither moves the outcome. Seat-2 (edgar-vampires) is NOT unchanged: Bloodthirsty Conqueror gains it 1 for the Crawler loss and 136 for the combat loss, Blood Artist 1 for Zombie 449 — at least 181 before the seven Blood Artist death triggers and their Conqueror echoes, whose targets are unrecorded. Craterhoof Behemoth dies to Grave Titan's deathtouch; your other ten attackers survive.
